content:
Thirty four years on, the first one is still shipping

In this issue

  • They were here first. Intershop was founded in 1992 in Jena, in what had been East Germany two years earlier, and it was not called Intershop.
  • Why so many of them are German. Working through the backlog for this series, I noticed something I had not gone looking for.
  • The agentic story. The shape of it, before the detail.
  • Who it is for, and who it is not for. For a mid-market European manufacturer, wholesaler, or distributor carrying a heavy aftersales and installed-base service load, who wants working AI assistance in production now without standing up an integration project, Intershop is a serious pick.
  • Verdict. Scored on paper, the same standard every platform gets in this series.
  • The founder left, the lesson stayed. Schambach got to start over. He took what Jena and San Francisco taught him to Massachusetts, built the same thing again with better timing, and sold it for two point eight billion dollars.
